pr_title: tests: pwm: led: Fix pwm_led sample
pr_body:
The PR fixes the pwm_led sample:
- now test doesn't rely on any specific device name
- Logs which are scanned with regex in the test are printed
  only after a command passes (before failures were not
  affecting the test verdict)
- If 1 sec cycle is not supported appropriate info is printed
  and won't cause the test to failed
- Changed second "Turned off" msg so regex doesn't mix it with the
  the first one.

Fixes #35524

Signed-off-by: Maciej Perkowski <Maciej.Perkowski@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments:
@anangl @simonguinot Thanks for you commments. Indeed, I focused on the test's point of view and forgot about the user experience. I believe I addressed all your comments. I brought 1 sec period back and added else case (and regex check) when such period is not supported.
In addition, I changed the log/check for the last "turned off" as it was possible it got mixed with the one from the beginning of the loop.

issue_context.title: tests: samples: led: LED PWM sample fails on nrf platforms
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The test sample.drivers.led.led_pwm from /zephyr/samples/drivers/led_pwm fails on nrf platforms. The printed output is:
```
DEBUG   - DEVICE: *** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v2.5.0-4044-g58d3760533a6  ***
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:00.445,037] <inf> main: Found device pwmleds
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:00.445,068] <inf> main: Testing LED 0 - no label
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:00.445,068] <inf> main:   Turning on
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:01.445,159] <inf> main:   Turning off
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:02.445,251] <inf> main:   Increasing brightness gradually
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:04.462,493] <inf> main:   Blinking on: 0.1 sec, off: 0.1 sec
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,585] <inf> main:   Blinking on: 1 sec, off: 1 sec
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <err> pwm_nrfx: Prescaler for period_cycles 32000000 not found.
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <err> main: err=-22
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <inf> main: Testing LED 0 - no label
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <inf> main:   Turning on
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:10.462,707] <inf> main:   Turning off
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:11.462,768] <inf> main:   Increasing brightness gradually
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:13.480,010] <inf> main:   Blinking on: 0.1 sec, off: 0.1 sec
DEBUG   - Timed out while monitoring serial output on nrf52dk_nrf52832
DEBUG   - run status: nrf52dk_nrf52832/samples/drivers/led_pwm/sample.drivers.led.led_pwm timeout
INFO    - 1/1 nrf52dk_nrf52832          samples/drivers/led_pwm/sample.drivers.led.led_pwm FAILED Timeout (device 18.206s)
```
It seems the device name was changed to `pwmleds`. The sample.yaml tells that `"Found device LED_PWM_\\d+"` is been looked for. Changing to `LED_PWM_` to `pwmleds` makes the sample pass. 

I can fix this by myself, however I am worried about these lines in the output:
```
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <err> pwm_nrfx: Prescaler for period_cycles 32000000 not found.
DEBUG   - DEVICE: [00:00:09.462,615] <err> main: err=-22
```
It reports an error, but the error is handled nowhere. Should the test be fixed to fail if there are such errors or is it "a feature"?

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. connect e.g. nrf52dk_nrf52832
2. run `./scripts/twister -T samples/drivers/led_pwm/ -p nrf52dk_nrf52832 --device-testing --device-serial /dev/ttyACM0 -v -v --inline-logs`
3. See error

**Expected behavior**
Test passes. Errors are handled properly

**Environment:**
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04
 - Toolchain zephyr-sdk 0.12.2
 - Commit SHA or Version used zephyr-v2.5.0-4044-g58d3760533a6


It seems like the PWM period is too long and it's not supported by the pwm_nrfx driver (hardware limitation).
Maybe we could just print information that it's not supported by the driver without marking this as an error?
I am not sure if it should be mandatory for PWM LED driver implementation to support so long periods for blink operation. Blink operation could be implemented using k_work_delayable that resubmits itself periodically aswell.

I belive updating the label in sample.yaml regex will make the test pass. I will provide a PR in a moment with the updated label.
It seems the error from the log (nrfx driver) is not treated as an error by twister. We will decide how to handle communicating that >0.25s periods are not supported by nrfx driver.

review_comments:
Hi @PerMac.

Please, keep this test.

Configuring the PWM for a LED is a trade-off. You want the PWM frequency as high as possible to fool eyes and camera on steady brightness levels. But on the other end, you also want the PWM configuration to support a 0.5 Hz hardware blinking which is a pretty common need. This test allows to verify that.

Concretely, on a ST board, this helps to check that the value assignated to "st,prescaler" DT property is correct.
